name: Banana Beach at Hijo Resorts Davao
description: Situated inside the 760-hectare Hijo banana and coconut plantation along the Davao Gulf, Banana Beach at Hijo Resorts Davao is the world's only beach resort set within a working banana plantation. The estate blends a dark-sand coastline, a beachfront infinity pool, and thatched-roof casitas with a protected secondary-growth forest reserve and the Madaum River estuary.
location: Hijo Plantation, Davao-Surigao Coastal Road, Barangay Madaum, Tagum City, 8100 Davao del Norte, Philippine
activities: Swimming in the oceanfront infinity pool, kayaking along the coast or mangrove river, Wild Forest Experience guided nature walks (spotting Philippine macaques, wild boars, and birds), River & Beach Cruise, banana plantation tours, horseback riding, cycling, and line fishing at The Spot.
best_time_to_visit: Early morning (8:00 AM – 10:30 AM) for cooler weather during forest, river, and plantation tours, or late afternoon (3:30 PM – 5:30 PM) for lounging by the beachfront infinity pool and watching sunsets over the Davao Gulf.
how_to_get_there:
• By Private Vehicle: From Carmen, drive toward Tagum City via the Daang Maharlika Highway (AH26), then turn south onto the Tagum–Mati / Davao-Surigao Coastal Road toward Barangay Madaum. Turn into the Hijo Plantation gate and follow the internal plantation road for about 5 to 10 minutes straight to the Banana Beach parking lot. Free parking is available on-site.

• By Public Transport: Ride a bus or van from Carmen to the Tagum City Overland Transport Integrated Terminal. Transfer to a jeepney, multicab, or bus heading toward Madaum / Maco / Mati and alight at the Hijo Plantation / Banana Beach gate in Madaum. From the main gate, hire a tricycle or habal-habal to take you through the plantation to the beachfront reception.
travel_notes: Manage Beach Water Expectations, No Outside Food & Drinks, Advance Reservations
what_to_bring: Proper swimwear (strictly required for the infinity pool), beach towel, reef-safe sunscreen, sunglasses, hat, mosquito repellent (especially for forest and river tours), comfortable walking shoes for plantation trails, extra dry clothes, and cash or e-wallet/card for on-site food and activity add-ons.

name: Chema's by the Sea
description: Nestled along a lush, tree-lined cove in Barangay Limao right next to Discovery Samal, Chema's by the Sea is an intimate nature-oriented beach resort featuring four rustic cabanas and six Balinese-inspired cottages.
location: Purok 5, Barangay Limao, Samal District, Island Garden City of Samal, 8119 Davao del Norte, Philippines. Mainland boat docking terminal: Waterfront Insular Hotel Davao Jetty, Lanang, Davao City.
category: Boutique Nature Beach Resort, Balinese-Style Island Retreat, and Pet-Friendly Hideaway.
activities: Swimming across three outdoor infinity pools and an Olympic-sized pool, lounging at the private white-sand beach, crystal kayaking and stand-up paddleboarding, motorized water sports (jet skiing, banana boat), beachfront pickleball, working out at Fit Studio, relaxing at Samal Escape Spa, children's arts and crafts at Sandbox, and dining at Morning Catch or The Bistro.
best_time_to_visit: Early morning (8:00 AM – 10:30 AM) or late afternoon (4:00 PM – 6:00 PM)
how_to_get_there:
• Step 1 — Reach Waterfront Insular Hotel Jetty (from Carmen): Drive south along the Daang Maharlika Highway (AH26) into Davao City (roughly 55 minutes to 1 hour 15 minutes depending on traffic) and proceed to Waterfront Insular Hotel Davao in Lanang. (By public transport, board a Davao-bound bus from Carmen, alight in Lanang near SM Lanang Premier, and take a short taxi or Grab to Waterfront Insular Hotel).

• Step 2 — Direct Resort Boat Transfer: Board the resort's private boat at the Waterfront Insular Hotel docking area. The scenic ride across the Davao Gulf to Chema's private wooden pier takes roughly 10 to 15 minutes (special off-schedule boat trips cost ₱1,500 per way).
travel_notes: Mandatory Full Prepayment & Scam Advisory, Pet-Friendly Policy, and No Outside Food & Drinks.
what_to_bring: • Valid government photo ID (required for registration at the Davao Welcome Center), proper swimwear, beach cover-up, reef-safe sunscreen, sunglasses and sunhat, smart-casual attire for upscale dining, and credit/debit cards or cash for incidentals and spa services.

name: Davao del Norte Sports and Tourism Complex (DNSTC)
description: A premier, 11-hectare government-run sports and leisure complex located inside the Davao del Norte Provincial Capitol Compound in Barangay Mankilam, Tagum City. It houses Olympic-standard facilities—including an 8-lane rubberized track oval, a 10-lane aquatic center, an air-conditioned gymnasium, and a cultural tourism village—that regularly host national and regional athletic meets alongside daily community fitness activities.
location: Capitol Circumferential Road. Provincial Government Center, Barangay Mankilam, Tagum City, 8105 Davao del Norte
activities: Track and field jogging or sprinting, lap swimming at the 50-meter Olympic pool, indoor basketball, volleyball, and badminton at the Rodolfo P. Del Rosario (RDR) Gymnasium, outdoor lawn tennis, archery, football, and shopping for local delicacies at the Tourism Village pasalubong center.
how_to_get_there:
By Private Vehicle: From Carmen, drive north along the Daang Maharlika Highway (AH26) for about 25 to 30 minutes, then turn onto Capitol Circumferential Road (Tagum City Diversion Road) in Barangay Mankilam to enter the Provincial Capitol Compound. Free parking is available on-site.

By Public Transport: Board any northbound bus (such as Bachelor Express) or commuter van from Carmen toward Tagum City and alight at the Capitol Junction / Mankilam intersection. From there, take a tricycle straight inside the Capitol Compound to the complex gates.
travel_notes:
• Public access to specific tracks, pools, or courts may be temporarily restricted during major regional or national sporting events (such as the DAVRAA Meet or Palarong Pambansa).
• Strict dress codes are enforced on specialized surfaces—standard street shoes or slippers are prohibited on the rubberized track oval, and proper swimming attire is mandatory at the pool.
what_to_bring: Proper rubber-soled athletic shoes (required for the track), proper swimwear and a swimming cap (if using the Aquatic Center), a reusable water bottle, a face towel, extra dry clothes, and small cash bills for facility fees and tricycles.

name: Discovery Samal
description: Located in Barangay Limao on the western coast of Samal Island directly across from Davao City, Discovery Samal is a sprawling 5-star luxury resort featuring 153 villas and suites, three tiered infinity pools, a full Olympic-sized pool, a private white-sand beachfront, and the largest resort convention center in Mindanao. Guests arrive via a dedicated 5-minute private speedboat ride from the resort's mainland Davao Welcome Center, enjoying panoramic views of the Davao Gulf and Mount Apo.
location: Barangay Limao, Island Garden City of Samal, 8119 Davao del Norte, Philippines.
category: 5-Star Luxury Beachfront Resort, Convention Hub, and Island Staycation Retreat.
activities: Swimming across three outdoor infinity pools and an Olympic-sized pool, lounging at the private white-sand beach, crystal kayaking and stand-up paddleboarding, motorized water sports (jet skiing, banana boat), beachfront pickleball, working out at Fit Studio, relaxing at Samal Escape Spa, children's arts and crafts at Sandbox, and dining at Morning Catch or The Bistro.
how_to_get_there:
• Step 1 — Reach the Davao Welcome Center (from Carmen): Drive south along the Daang Maharlika Highway (AH26) into Davao City (roughly 55 minutes to 1 hour 15 minutes depending on traffic) and head to the Discovery Samal Davao Welcome Center along Maryknoll Drive, Lanang/Buhangin (near Waterfront Insular Hotel). Free parking is available on-site. (By public transport, take a Davao-bound bus from Carmen, alight in Lanang near SM Lanang Premier, and ride a short taxi or Grab to the Davao Welcome Center).

• Step 2 — Private Resort Boat Transfer: Check in at the Davao Welcome Center lounge and board the resort's private speedboat. The direct crossing to the resort's private jetty takes only 5 minutes.
travel_notes: Mandatory Advance Reservations & Scam Advisory, Strict Beach & Pool Access Rules, Mandatory Environmental Fee, and No Outside Food & Drinks.
what_to_bring: Valid government photo ID (required for registration at the Davao Welcome Center), proper swimwear, beach cover-up, reef-safe sunscreen, sunglasses and sunhat, smart-casual attire for upscale dining, and credit/debit cards or cash for incidentals and spa services.

name: LYR Agro Inland Resort
description: Set across an expansive 80-hectare property in Upper La Filipina, LYR Agro Inland Resort combines a working grape vineyard (growing over a dozen grape varieties) with a 2-hectare man-made lake, a large swimming pool complex (LYR Agro Aqua Pools), pickleball courts, and open-air event spaces.
location: Purok 8, Upper La Filipina, Tagum City, 8100 Davao del Norte, Philippines
category: Agritourism Vineyard, Inland Pool Resort, and Family Recreational Park.
activities: Swimming at LYR Agro Aqua Pools, pedal boating and water rides on the 2-hectare man-made lake, touring the grape vineyard and buying locally produced grape wine (~₱300/bottle), fish feeding, cycling, playing pickleball, photo-ops with giant statues, and dining at the on-site restaurant.
best_time_to_visit: Early morning (8:30 AM – 10:30 AM) or late afternoon (3:30 PM – 6:00 PM)
how_to_get_there:

Wheelchair-accessible parking is available on-site.

	• By Public Transport: Ride a northbound bus or van from Carmen to Tagum City, alight at the city center or terminal, and hire a tricycle or habal-habal (motorcycle taxi) to take you up to Purok 8, Upper La Filipina (confirm the pakyaw fare with the driver beforehand since it is in the upper barangay area).
travel_notes: Separate Fees by Zone, Ongoing Expansion, and Check Weekend Promos.
what_to_bring: Proper swimwear (if using the swimming pool), extra dry clothes and a towel, comfortable non-slip walking shoes or sandals (pathways can be damp near the lake and pool), sun protection (hat, sunglasses, sunscreen), and cash in small bills for entrance fees, boat rides, and tricycles.

name: Lanikai Hijo Estate Resort
description: Located inside the sprawling 760-hectare Hijo Plantation along the Davao Gulf, Lanikai (Hawaiian for "heaven by the sea") is the renovated two-story American-colonial ancestral heritage house of the Tuason family converted into an intimate, 8-room boutique resort.
location: Lanikai, Hijo Plantation (Hijo Estates), Davao-Surigao Coastal Road, Barangay Madaum, Tagum City, 8100 Davao del Norte, Philippines.
activities: • Swimming in the oceanfront infinity pool, kayaking and stand-up paddleboarding on the Davao Gulf, "catch-your-own-protein" line fishing at The Spot (which the kitchen can cook for dinner), cycling through the coconut and banana groves on mountain bikes, billiards, stargazing, horseback riding, and joining guided Wild Forest or River & Beach Cruise tours.
best_time_to_visit: Overnight Guests: Open 24 hours; standard check-in is 2:00 PM and check-out is 12:00 PM.
how_to_get_there:
• By Private Vehicle: From Carmen, drive toward Tagum City along the Daang Maharlika Highway (AH26), then turn south onto the Tagum–Mati / Davao-Surigao Coastal Road toward Barangay Madaum. Enter the Hijo Plantation main gate, inform the security guard of your Lanikai booking, and follow the shaded plantation road to the beachfront heritage house. On-site parking is free.

	• By Public Transport: Take a northbound bus or van from Carmen to the Tagum City Overland Transport Integrated Terminal, transfer to a jeepney, multicab, or bus bound for Madaum / Maco / Mati, and alight at the Hijo Plantation gate in Madaum. From the gate, hire a tricycle or habal-habal to take you inside the estate to Lanikai (or arrange a private resort transfer in advance).
travel_notes: Reservation-Only Exclusivity, Estuary Shoreline, and No Outside Food.
what_to_bring: Proper swimwear (required for the infinity pool), beach towel, sunglasses, sunblock, mosquito repellent (for forest and river tours), comfortable walking shoes or sandals, smart-casual attire for dinner on the veranda, and cash or cards for incidental bills and activity add-ons.

name: Paradise Island Park & Beach Resort
description: Located on the western shore of Samal Island directly facing Davao City, Paradise Island Park & Beach Resort is one of Samal's longest-running and most accessible beachfront resorts. It features an 800-meter stretch of groomed white sand, a protected 300-meter shallow coral reef ("Paradise Reef"), manicured tropical gardens, a mini-zoo and aviary ("Bird Country"), and open-air beachfront dining halls—all connected via a 5-to-10-minute ride on the resort's private pump boats from Sasa, Davao City.
location: Barangay Caliclic, Babak District, Island Garden City of Samal, 8119 Davao del Norte, Philippines
category: Classic Beachfront Resort, Family Eco-Park, and Day-Tour Island Getaway.
activities: Swimming along the white-sand beach, snorkeling over Paradise Reef, kayaking (including crystal kayaks), aqua biking, stand-up paddleboarding, jet skiing and banana boat rides, visiting the Bird Country aviary and mini-zoo, fish feeding, beach volleyball, indoor games (billiards, ping-pong, air hockey, foosball), relaxing at Alima Spa, and watching live acoustic bands or weekend fireworks.
how_to_get_there:
• Step 1 — Reach Km. 9 Sasa Port (from Carmen): Drive south along the Daang Maharlika Highway (AH26) into Davao City (roughly 55 minutes to 1 hour 10 minutes depending on traffic) and turn into Km. 9, Sasa right beside the public Sasa Ferry Terminal. Secure, free parking is available at the resort's mainland dock. (By public transport, board a Davao-bound bus from Carmen, alight in Sasa near Km. 9, and walk or take a short tricycle/pedicab to the Paradise Island boat terminal).

• Step 2 — Direct Resort Pump Boat: Board one of the resort's colorful private pump boats directly at the Sasa dock—no need to queue for the public barge. The crossing takes just 5 to 10 minutes.
travel_notes: Strict No Outside Food & Drinks Policy, Valid ID Required and Boat Minimums.
what_to_bring: Valid government photo ID, swimwear and rash guard, beach towel, reef-safe sunscreen, sunglasses and wide-brimmed hat, personal snorkeling mask/snorkel (or rent on-site), dry clothes, and cash (plus e-wallet/card) for entrance fees, restaurant meals, and water sports.

name: Pearl Farm Beach Resort
description: Located on a secluded cove on the southwest side of the Island Garden City of Samal (including the private islet of Isla Malipano), Pearl Farm Beach Resort is a former South Sea pearl farm transformed into Mindanao's most iconic luxury island sanctuary. Masterfully designed by National Artist Francisco "Bobby" Mañosa, its overwater Samal Houses, hilltop suites, and beachfront villas showcase indigenous Moro and Lumad architectural heritage set beside white-sand coves, infinity pools, and vibrant coral reefs.
location: Barangay Adecor, Kaputian District (Babak–Samal–Kaputian Road), Island Garden City of Samal, 8119 Davao del Norte, Philippines (Mainland boat terminal: Pearl Farm Marina Wharf, Lizada Street, Lanang, Davao City).
activities: • Snorkeling along the house coral reef and marine sanctuary, kayaking, canoeing, and stand-up paddleboarding, motorized water sports (jet skiing, banana boat, scuba diving, and windsurfing), island-hopping to the Taklobo (Giant Clam) Sanctuary, swimming in the beachfront infinity pools, playing tennis or beach volleyball, relaxing at the Mandaya Spa, and enjoying sunset drinks at Parola Bar.
how_to_get_there:
• Step 1 — Reach the Mainland Marina (from Carmen): Drive south along the Daang Maharlika Highway (AH26) into Davao City (roughly 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes depending on traffic) and proceed to Pearl Farm Marina Wharf on Lizada Street, Lanang. (By public transport, take a Davao-bound bus from Carmen, alight in Lanang near SM Lanang Premier, and take a taxi or Grab to Pearl Farm Marina Wharf).

	• Step 2 — Private Resort Boat Transfer: Check in at the Marina lounge at least 30 minutes before your scheduled boat departure. The scenic resort motorboat ride across the Davao Gulf takes approximately 45 minutes. (Alternatively, you can take the public Sasa–Babak ferry to Samal Island and drive/hire a private van south along the Babak–Samal–Kaputian Road, though the direct Marina boat is standard for resort guests).
travel_notes: Mandatory Advance Booking & Scam Warning, All-Inclusive Overnight Model, Day Tour Restrictions, and Facility Advisory.
what_to_bring: Valid government photo ID and the physical credit card used for online booking (required at Marina check-in), proper swimwear, rash guard and reef-safe sunscreen, personal snorkeling gear (if preferred over resort rentals), sunglasses and sunhat, smart-casual resort wear for evening dining, and cash or card for motorized water sports and spa treatments.

name: Tagum City Historical & Cultural center
description: Built on the site of the former Old City Hall in downtown Tagum, this modern, music-inspired landmark is crowned by a giant G-clef facade honoring Tagum as the "Music Capital of Mindanao".
location: Rizal Street, Barangay Magupo Poblacion, Tagum City, 8100 Davao Del Norte
category: Cultural Center, Heritage Museum, Public Library, and Performing Arts Venue.
activities: Touring the Kagikan Museum (pre-colonial history, indigenous instruments, and heritage replicas), browsing local paintings at the ground-floor art gallery, reading or studying at the City Library and Learning Commons, watching cultural performances at Tagumpay Theater, and strolling around Freedom Park.
best_time_to_visit: Thursday mornings (9:00 AM – 11:30 AM) when the center offers free guided historical tours.
how_to_get_there:
• By Private Vehicle: From Carmen, drive north along the Daang Maharlika Highway (AH26) for about 25 to 30 minutes into Tagum City proper, then turn toward Rizal Street / Magugpo Poblacion (adjacent to Freedom Park and near Christ the King Cathedral). Wheelchair-accessible parking is available on-site.

	• By Public Transport: Ride a northbound bus or commuter van from Carmen to Tagum City. Alight along the highway in the city center (or at the Tagum Overland Transport Terminal) and take a short tricycle ride directly to the Old City Hall / Freedom Park along Rizal Street.
travel_notes:
• Admission to the museum, library, and galleries is free.
	• Visitors must deposit large bags at the baggage counter before entering the museum.
	• No flash photography and no touching of artifacts are strictly enforced inside the Kagikan Museum.
	• The building features full wheelchair accessibility (entrance, restrooms, and parking).
what_to_bring: A valid ID (for visitor log-in and baggage check), a light jacket or cardigan (the indoor museum and library air-conditioning is quite cold), a fully charged phone or camera (for non-flash gallery photos and exterior shots), and small cash bills for nearby snacks.

name: Tagum City River Cruise / Nabintad River
description: An 8.8-kilometer protected mangrove river system and wetland conservation site stretching through coastal Tagum City (Barangay Madaum and Barangay Liboganon).
location: Purok 1C, Nabintad, Barangay Madaum, Tagum City, Davao del Norte (Plus Code: 9R84+HQ, Tagum) for Nabintad Riverside Park; the main Tagum / Liboganon River Cruise Station is located in adjacent Barangay Liboganon (Plus Code: 9Q78+4QF, Tagum).
activities: Motorized riverboat mangrove tours, kayaking, hand-paddled boat rides, stand-up paddleboarding, relaxing in floating cottages, recreational line fishing (bring your own rod), birdwatching, and tasting native kakanin and brewed coffee from riverside stalls.
best_time_to_visit: Early morning (7:00 AM – 9:30 AM) for cool weather and birdwatching, or mid-to-late afternoon (3:00 PM – 5:00 PM) during high tide, when the river water is deepest, clearest, and easiest for kayaking and motorboat cruising.
how_to_get_there:
• By Private Vehicle: From Carmen, drive south/southeast toward Tagum City along the Daang Maharlika Highway (AH26), then turn onto the Tagum–Mati Road / Maco Highway heading toward Barangay Madaum. Turn off the highway onto the paved barangay road leading into Purok 1C, Nabintad (roughly 1 km off the main highway). On-site parking is available.

• By Public Transport: Ride a bus or van from Carmen to the Tagum City Overland Transport Integrated Terminal. From there, transfer to a jeepney, multicab, or van bound for Madaum / Maco / Mati, alight at the Nabintad / Madaum junction, and take a short tricycle or habal-habal ride straight to Nabintad Riverside Park.
travel_notes: Cultural & Community Rules, Advance Booking for Large Cruises, and Check Tide Levels
what_to_bring: Modest outdoor clothing and swimwear (rash guards and board shorts/leggings), sunscreen, a wide-brimmed hat or sunglasses, mosquito repellent, a waterproof dry bag for phones and wallets, extra dry clothes, and cash in small bills (no ATMs or digital payment terminals on-site).
